dedupe_keys.name: stop bad data centers policy tracker state and federal data centre legislation

description: The Stop Bad Data Centers policy tracker is an interactive library of current legislation affecting data centre development at state and federal level. Each bill entry gives a plain-language title and summary, the state or federal jurisdiction and session, the bill status (introduced, in committee, in chamber, passed one chamber, passed both chambers, vetoed, adopted, enacted, substituted or died), the party of the lead sponsors and a link to the legislation. The tracker covers bills from moratoria on new data centres to water and energy reporting requirements, repeals or conditions on tax breaks and rate-protection measures that keep data centre costs off household bills, plus pre-emption bills, critical infrastructure carve-outs and expanded tax incentives; a legend defines the concerns, objectives and methods such as capacity and capital investment. Producer: the Halt the Harm Network, an advocacy group, with briefings by an independent tech policy analyst. Coverage: US states and federal level. Access: a public web page; login is only needed for comments. Licence and cost: free; no licence stated. Caveats: run by an advocacy group, so the selection and framing reflect that perspective, and status may lag the legislatures. Simulation uses: bill status and content feed scenario assumptions on data centre load growth, energy and water reporting. Related record: the DC Map policy tracker (data-dcmap-us-data-center-policy-tracker).
